title: Liverpool’s Rio Ngumoha keen on ‘more minutes’ after star cameo in Nottingham Forest win
content:
Rio Ngumoha is keen for “more minutes” in Liverpool’s first team after his impressive cameo in Sunday’s 1-0 win over Nottingham Forest.

The 17-year-old, who has yet to make a Premier League start, has made a big impact off the bench in the victory at the City Ground.

Ngumoha has featured in every competition for Liverpool this season, but 11 of his 14 appearances have come as a late substitute.

When asked if he’s aiming for additional game-time in the remainder of the campaign, the teenager said: “Yeah, hopefully soon. I just need to keep pushing and keep gaining the manager’s trust and hopefully that leads to more minutes.”

The winger earned praise for his cameo on Sunday from from head coach Arne Slot, who said he was pleased with the youngster’s contributions and explained how his development is rapidly excelling.

Ngumoha added: “I think it has gone really well. I am learning a lot every day and playing with and training with some of the best players in the world.

“I can’t ask for much more as a young kid. So I just think I need to carry on proving, working hard in training and showing what I can do to the manager. I just try to help the team. It’s all I can do, just put balls into the box whenever the manager needs me.”

Ngumoha, signed from Chelsea in September 2024, has never been called upon before the 70-minute mark of a Premier League game this season, and has only been introduced when Liverpool are chasing a late goal.

He says the game state affects the demands, but enjoys the challenge of taking on and beating opponents.

“I know I need to at least do something and try and impact the game,” he says.

“Whether that is on the ball or off the ball. So whether it is like trying to put in a tackle or press to win the ball back, put balls into the box, have shots on target or just beat my man. Every single time I am called on for the team, I just want to show everyone what I can do.

“Obviously if it is 0-0 you’ve got to be a little bit less expressive. However, if the opportunity is there to take on a man, I will do it any day of the week.”

Ngumoha says Slot and the coaching team have been holding individual meetings with him to analyse performance in training, and he is also open to playing more under-21 games.

“I feel like if you are not playing as much then you can stagnate,” he added. “So I am available to play any games.”
